title: HiCOT: Improving Neural Topic Models via Optimal Transport and Contrastive Learning
subcategory: embedding-based NTM with optimal transport and hierarchical-clustering contrastive learning
task: Topic modelling on long and short text collections
problem: NTMs show weak document-topic alignment, high inference cost when large PLMs are used, and limited modelling of topic-topic structure.
architecture: Doc2Vec document embeddings are projected by an MLP into the topic-embedding space and aligned with topic embeddings by entropic optimal transport; a second OT term aligns topic proportions with document semantic relationships; hierarchical agglomerative clustering groups topic embeddings, and triplet contrastive losses act on words within topics and between topics of a cluster.
key_results: GoogleNews, K = 100: Purity 0.763 and NMI 0.864 vs 0.664 and 0.834 for NeuroMax.
strengths: Outperforms PLM-based models while using lightweight Doc2Vec embeddings, giving faster inference than FASTopic.
Contrastive loss choice (triplet, InfoNCE, Circle) has little effect, indicating robustness.

limitations.text: The interval for re-clustering topics must be tuned; too long slows convergence.
Choice of positive and negative samples for contrastive learning remains open.
Topic diversity is not always best (20NG, K = 50: TD 0.852 vs 0.980 for FASTopic).

notes: Several baseline numbers are copied from earlier papers (marked in the paper).
